headline: Calibrated models extend genetic association, fine-mapping and variant effect prediction
label: Genetic Association Inference Methods
summary: Calibration, interaction structure and phenotype resolution are now central as association methods scale to biobank and single-cell data.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the statistical and biological validity of inference from genetic association data. The SuSiE 2.0 preprint redesigns fine-mapping software for extensibility, adds up to 5x faster summary-statistics runs, and introduces SuSiE-ash for better calibration. Published work extends this toward interaction-aware modelling: a comparison of interaction and variance polygenic scores for PGS×BMI effects in UK Biobank and All of Us, and a systems genomics model of cumulative non-coding SNP effects across 2,636 IBD patients. Molecular phenotype resolution is addressed by BASIC, which decomposes bulk eQTL effects along cell-type axes to boost power and GWAS colocalization for brain traits, and by distQTL, which applies Fréchet regression to full single-cell expression distributions in OneK1K. Variant interpretation is covered by popEVE, V2P and a DNA foundation model benchmark. What is new is the pairing of calibrated, interaction-aware modelling with finer molecular phenotypes, though the items do not share a single methodological framework.
